facts.value: GPT-5.4-Cyber: fine-tuned GPT-5.4 with deliberately lower refusal threshold for legitimate defensive prompts (vuln research, binary reverse engineering without source); access requires strong KYC/identity verification (individuals at chatgpt.com/cyber, enterprises via OpenAI rep). Hard prohibitions on exfiltration/malware/destructive testing remain at every tier; cannot run in zero-data-retention environments (OpenAI requires visibility into user/environment/intent).

Operates a Verified-Organization ID-gating regime for advanced/reasoning/streaming models: government photo ID from permitted countries + org affiliation proof; each ID verifies one org per 90-day window. Rolled out April 2025; gates Tier 1-3 (Tier 4-5 exempt).

OpenAI released GPT-5.5-Cyber ('roughly on par with Mythos') around the Glasswing expansion (limited preview May 7 2026); extended it to vetted European defenders, businesses, governments, cyber agencies and EU institutions incl. the EU AI Office via Trusted Access for Cyber (EU plan announced ~May 11 2026 by AI Policy Lead Martin Signoux), ahead of and contrasting with Anthropic's slower European rollout. Anthropic framed restricted Glasswing as a race to set safeguards before rivals ship comparable cyber models (expected within 6-12 months).

OpenAI released GPT-5.5 on April 23 2026 (its smartest, most intuitive model): handles messy multi-part agentic tasks, excels at agentic coding/knowledge work/math/scientific research, matches GPT-5.4 per-token latency while using significantly fewer tokens on Codex tasks.

On Apr 14 2026 (Axios first) OpenAI expanded Trusted Access for Cyber (TAC) into 3 tiers: (1) baseline, (2) trusted access to existing models with less friction for legitimate security work, (3) higher tier giving vetted defenders GPT-5.4-Cyber. Shifts cyber-risk control from restricting what models can do to verifying WHO gets access.

GPT-5.5 variants: Thinking & Pro (2026-04-23, paid), Instant (2026-05-05, free-tier default replacing GPT-5.3), Cyber (limited preview 2026-05-07 for vetted cyber teams); API opened 2026-04-24. Benchmarks: Terminal-Bench 2.0 82.7%, FrontierMath Tier 1-3 51.7% / Tier 4 35.4%; UK AI Security Institute reported 71.4% pass on expert-level cyber tasks (potentially strongest it had tested).

OpenAI rolled out tiered access to advanced AI cyber models in April 2026, shifting focus from restricting model capabilities to 'verifying who gets access to the most sensitive capabilities' through identity verification and monitoring. This is a parallel, company-driven access-gating trend distinct from but structurally adjacent to the government-mandated Anthropic nationality restriction.

OpenAI's 'Verified Organization' system, introduced April 2025, requires developers to submit government-issued ID from OpenAI-permitted countries to access the most advanced models. Each ID verifies only one organization per 90 days. This is voluntary, company-driven nationality-adjacent gating — not mandated by the US government — predating the Anthropic June 2026 directive.

narration.text: A three-day worldline. Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 launch on 2026-06-09 and are cut on 2026-06-12 at 17:21 ET - the first time a leading AI company takes a publicly deployed model offline under US federal intervention. What follows is told only from what the substrate holds; confidence and route travel with each line.

July 23 2025: the administration released 'America's AI Action Plan' + an EO 'Promoting the Export of the American AI Technology Stack,' pivoting from Biden-era guardrails to deregulatory 'green lights' — full-stack AI export packages to allies, targeting state AI-law preemption, and (via BIS) rescinding the AI Diffusion Rule. Followed by chip oscillation: blocked H20 (Apr 2025), resumed H20/MI308 (Jul 2025), 15% China-sale revenue-share (Aug 2025), H200 to vetted Chinese customers (Dec 2025), ~10 firms cleared by May 2026, and a June 1 2026 BIS move closing the foreign-subsidiary loophole for China-HQ'd firms.

Feb 27 / early-Mar 2026: the Pentagon under Defense Sec. Hegseth designated Anthropic a 'supply-chain risk' (label historically reserved for foreign/hostile entities, never before a domestic US company; via FASCSA / Title 41 Sec. 4713) with a six-month phase-out, after Anthropic refused weapons/surveillance uses. Stemmed from failed renegotiation of the July 2025 contract. The dispute also drew in Treasury (under Bessent) discontinuing Anthropic products.

Feb 27 2026: President Trump directed federal agencies to 'IMMEDIATELY CEASE all use of Anthropic's technology'; after a Friday 5:01 PM ET deadline, ordered a government-wide six-month phase-out. White House spokeswoman Liz Huston: the president 'will never allow a radical left, woke company to jeopardize our national security' and military operations must follow 'the United States Constitution — not any woke AI company's terms.'

Rozenshtein (w/ Michael Endrias) co-authored Lawfare's 'Pentagon's Anthropic Designation Won't Survive First Contact with Legal System' (Mar 2026) arguing the designation exceeds 10 U.S.C. 3252 (covert foreign sabotage/subversion, not transparent contract terms), violates due process (no notice/hearing) and is pretextual First Amendment retaliation; and 'The Right Remedy in the Anthropic Case' (Mar 19 2026) recommending Lin enjoin the Sec. 3252 designation + secondary boycott while preserving ordinary procurement discretion. He filed an amicus and predicted the Commerce ban could be 'the first big First Amendment AI case,' while warning against treating all AI output as protected speech.

Anthropic filed suit on/around Mar 9 2026 in N.D. Cal. (48-page complaint, plus a D.C. Circuit petition + emergency stay) alleging the supply-chain-risk designation is 'arbitrary, capricious, an abuse of discretion, and contrary to law' and unconstitutional First Amendment retaliation/viewpoint discrimination: 'The Constitution does not allow the government to wield its enormous power to punish a company for its protected speech.' Also alleges APA and due-process violations; FIRE and Cato filed amici arguing 'Claude is fundamentally expressive' and removing safeguards is compelled speech.

Tillipman characterized the sequence as improper: 'The President tweeted, then the Secretary tweeted, then the Department reverse-engineered an administrative record to backfill the justification,' calling corporate exclusion 'the corporate death penalty' warranting FAR 9.4 safeguards (notice, opportunity to respond, insulated officials) that were absent.

Judge Rita Lin (N.D. Cal., Biden appointee) granted Anthropic a preliminary injunction (Mar 26 2026; some sources Mar 27, hearing Mar 24) against the Pentagon supply-chain-risk designation, finding the record 'strongly suggests' the reasons were 'pretextual' and the real motive 'unlawful retaliation'; 'classic illegal First Amendment retaliation'; that an American company cannot be branded 'a potential adversary' for disagreeing (the 'Orwellian notion' line); 43/48-page order barring 17 federal agencies with a 7-day stay; restored federal Claude access incl. prior conversation histories (e.g., HHS). DOJ moved to appeal.

Emil Michael (Undersecretary of Defense / Pentagon CTO) responded to Lin's injunction on X that it contained 'dozens of factual errors' and the supply-chain-risk designation remained 'in full force and effect' under Title 41 Sec. 4713, claiming it fell outside her jurisdiction.

April 7 2026 (same day Mythos Preview was announced): unauthorized users accessed Claude Mythos Preview via a third-party vendor environment by guessing the model URL from Anthropic's endpoint naming conventions; a small group coordinated via a private Discord tracking unreleased models, and an individual at a third-party contractor appears to have facilitated access. Anthropic said no evidence of impact beyond the vendor environment.

Litigation split across two courts: N.D. Cal. granted a preliminary injunction (late Mar 2026), while on Apr 8 2026 the D.C. Circuit (panel Henderson/Katsas/Rao) DENIED Anthropic's emergency motion to stay but expedited a merits hearing — a 'same prompt, different responses' split. At the May 19 oral argument the panel appeared skeptical of the Pentagon's authority and 'remote kill switch' claim.

This is evaluation access only — not nationality gating or export restrictions on end users.
